All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:

Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-1070: [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)

## Description

## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).

  "fields": {
    "summary": "[GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)",
    "description": "## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).

# gh-1070: [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)

## Description

## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

## References

- dmtools-agents#1057 (dead-head park fork-blindness — merged; this card is its update-side sibling)
- Live incident: fa PR #1591, silent-update failures 2026-10-18 19:43–19:47Z, `silent-update-degraded`
- gh-757 (guest park), gh-1000 I5 (silent-update failure bookkeeping)

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. `smAgent` only probes and executes. - **One shared resolver** `smProvider.ghPrMaintainerCanModify` (REST `maintainer_can_modify` + GraphQL `maintainerCanModify` dialects, `null` when absent) consumed by `githubSource` on the PR item — the gh-1059 no-drift pattern; a reset in the same tick yields to the re-query instead of re-parking. - **AC4**: same-repo heads return `route: 'base'` without even paying the probe API call; the base repush command is byte-identical to the pre-gh-1070 form (regression test pins it). ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js # full suite (run_all.json manifest): 4531 passed, 0 failed ``` New coverage: routing dialects (UT-1), fork push URL never targets the base (UT-2), non-editable park with zero markers (UT-3/AC2), end-to-end BEHIND fork refresh + park clear (IT-1/AC1), AC3 exhaustion loop over 4 simulated ticks, same-repo regression (AC4), two-fork mixed tick. ### Known residual (out of scope) The gh-852 placeholder-reset lane still uses the classic base-only `silentUpdateBranchTracked`; # gh-1070: [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)

## Description

## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

## References

- dmtools-agents#1057 (dead-head park fork-blindness — merged; this card is its update-side sibling)
- Live incident: fa PR #1591, silent-update failures 2026-10-18 19:43–19:47Z, `silent-update-degraded`
- gh-757 (guest park), gh-1000 I5 (silent-update failure bookkeeping)

Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. # gh-1070: [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)

## Description

## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

## References

- dmtools-agents#1057 (dead-head park fork-blindness — merged; this card is its update-side sibling)
- Live incident: fa PR #1591, silent-update failures 2026-10-18 19:43–19:47Z, `silent-update-degraded`
- gh-757 (guest park), gh-1000 I5 (silent-update failure bookkeeping)

{
  "key": "gh-1070",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "[GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)",
    "description": "## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

## References

- dmtools-agents#1057 (dead-head park fork-blindness — merged; this card is its update-side sibling)
- Live incident: fa PR #1591, silent-update failures 2026-10-18 19:43–19:47Z, `silent-update-degraded`
- gh-757 (guest park), gh-1000 I5 (silent-update failure bookkeeping)

# gh-1070: [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)

## Description

## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

## References

- dmtools-agents#1057 (dead-head park fork-blindness — merged; this card is its update-side sibling)
- Live incident: fa PR #1591, silent-update failures 2026-10-18 19:43–19:47Z, `silent-update-degraded`
- gh-757 (guest park), gh-1000 I5 (silent-update failure bookkeeping)

  "fields": {
    "summary": "[GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)",
    "description": "## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. # gh-1070: [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)

## Description

## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. # Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1072 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1072 - **Title**: gh-1070 [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify fall back to guest park) - **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot] - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1070` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 9 - **Additions**: +653 - **Deletions**: -15 - **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:56:52Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-18T21:56:52Z ## PR Description Closes #1070 ### What changed `update_branch`'s silent refresh is now fork-aware (gh-1070): a cross-repo PR head is probed for `maintainerCanModify` before any update attempt — an editable fork gets main merged into its fork branch via the maintainer-edit push (`refs/pull//head` fetch → merge `origin/main` → push `HEAD:` to the fork's token URL), a non-editable fork parks guest-style with zero attempts and zero bookkeeping, and same-repo PRs ride the untouched base repush. ### Key decisions - **Pure dispatch** in `validationLiveness` (`forkSilentUpdateRoute` → `base` / `fork` / `park`, `forkPushTokenUrl`) — the three-path routing is unit-testable without scm stubs (UT-1/UT-2); `smAgent` only probes and executes. - **One shared resolver** `smProvider.ghPrMaintainerCanModify` (REST `maintainer_can_modify` + GraphQL `maintainerCanModify` dialects, `null` when absent) consumed by `githubSource` on the PR item — the gh-1059 no-drift pattern; an unknown probe fails **closed to the park path**, never an unprobed attempt. - **AC3 race**: a push that fails despite the probe rides the existing silent-update marker trail (counted once per tick, re-probe next tick); # gh-1070: [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)

## Description

## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

## References

- dmtools-agents#1057 (dead-head park fork-blindness — merged; this card is its update-side sibling)
- Live incident: fa PR #1591, silent-update failures 2026-10-18 19:43–19:47Z, `silent-update-degraded`
- gh-757 (guest park), gh-1000 I5 (silent-update failure bookkeeping)

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). # gh-1070: [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)

## Description

## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

## References

- dmtools-agents#1057 (dead-head park fork-blindness — merged; this card is its update-side sibling)
- Live incident: fa PR #1591, silent-update failures 2026-10-18 19:43–19:47Z, `silent-update-degraded`
- gh-757 (guest park), gh-1000 I5 (silent-update failure bookkeeping)

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
