# gh-1070: [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)

## Description

## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

## References

- dmtools-agents#1057 (dead-head park fork-blindness — merged; this card is its update-side sibling)
- Live incident: fa PR #1591, silent-update failures 2026-10-18 19:43–19:47Z, `silent-update-degraded`
- gh-757 (guest park), gh-1000 I5 (silent-update failure bookkeeping)

    "summary": "[GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)",
    "description": "## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-1070: [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)

## Description

## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

{
  "key": "gh-1070",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "[GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)",
    "description": "## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e

# gh-1070: [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)

## Description

## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

## References

- dmtools-agents#1057 (dead-head park fork-blindness — merged; this card is its update-side sibling)
- Live incident: fa PR #1591, silent-update failures 2026-10-18 19:43–19:47Z, `silent-update-degraded`
- gh-757 (guest park), gh-1000 I5 (silent-update failure bookkeeping)

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e

# gh-1070: [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)

## Description

## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

## References

- dmtools-agents#1057 (dead-head park fork-blindness — merged; this card is its update-side sibling)
- Live incident: fa PR #1591, silent-update failures 2026-10-18 19:43–19:47Z, `silent-update-degraded`
- gh-757 (guest park), gh-1000 I5 (silent-update failure bookkeeping)

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e

The lane starts at the top — the gh-994 head-change reset: the parked-head comment records the head sha; head hasn't moved → no reset. Then the guest red-head park check: label already present → skip. Then `forkSilentUpdateGate()`: forkFull non-null, probe → maintainerCanModify true (payload) → `{refresh: true}` → push attempted again → fails → recordForkSilentUpdateFailure: attempt = MAX+1 → no marker; left=0 → label already present → skip park; error log. And the validate_pr lane excludes validation_failed tickets, but update_branch BEHIND doesn't exclude parked tickets — for the classic path, parked tickets DO get silent-updated? Let me think about the classic semantics: the gh-757 park waits on the human author... but the BEHIND lane would still refresh the branch (that's how the machine helps: "a silent main-merge clears the park"). Indeed the park comment says "ANY push that moves the head (yours, the kicker, a silent main-merge) clears the park" — so the classic lane DOES keep refreshing parked PRs, intentionally: the machine merge moves the head → clears park. That's by design (the machine can still heal a red-head-parked PR by merging main).

For the AC3 fork case: the permission is gone, so refresh can never succeed — every tick burns a full clone+fetch+push against the fork and logs an error, forever, never healing. AC3's intent ("parks guest-style") implies the PR should then wait like a gh-757 park — but gh-757 parks wait for the AUTHOR push because the machine can't push. Here the machine can't push either (permission gone). Yet nothing stops the retry loop. Compare: classic I5 degraded path also retries every tick ("The retry itself stays every-tick (self-healing by design)") — but for the classic path the retry CAN succeed (transient network). For AC3 park, retry can succeed if the author re-enables edits — actually yes! # gh-1070: [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)

## Description

## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

## References

- dmtools-agents#1057 (dead-head park fork-blindness — merged; this card is its update-side sibling)
- Live incident: fa PR #1591, silent-update failures 2026-10-18 19:43–19:47Z, `silent-update-degraded`
- gh-757 (guest park), gh-1000 I5 (silent-update failure bookkeeping)

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e

# gh-1070: [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)

## Description

## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

## References

- dmtools-agents#1057 (dead-head park fork-blindness — merged; this card is its update-side sibling)
- Live incident: fa PR #1591, silent-update failures 2026-10-18 19:43–19:47Z, `silent-update-degraded`
- gh-757 (guest park), gh-1000 I5 (silent-update failure bookkeeping)

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"

Key observation about my earlier concern (perpetual attempts after AC3 park): after `recordForkSilentUpdateFailure` parks the PR (validation_failed added), what happens on subsequent ticks in the update_branch BEHIND lane? The lane starts at the top — the gh-994 head-change reset: the parked-head comment records the head sha; head hasn't moved → no reset. Then the guest red-head park check: label already present → skip. Then `forkSilentUpdateGate()`: forkFull non-null, probe → maintainerCanModify true (payload) → `{refresh: true}` → push attempted again → fails → recordForkSilentUpdateFailure: attempt = MAX+1 → no marker; left=0 → label already present → skip park; error log. So yes — after AC3 exhaustion, the machine keeps cloning/pushing every tick forever, each failing, with just a console.error. 

Wait — but is the ticket still matched by the BEHIND query? Yes, head still BEHIND. And the validate_pr lane excludes validation_failed tickets, but update_branch BEHIND doesn't exclude parked tickets — for the classic path, parked tickets DO get silent-updated? Let me think about the classic semantics: the gh-757 park waits on the human author... but the BEHIND lane would still refresh the branch (that's how the machine helps: "a silent main-merge clears the park"). Indeed the park comment says "ANY push that moves the head (yours, the kicker, a silent main-merge) clears the park" — so the classic lane DOES keep refreshing parked PRs, intentionally: the machine merge moves the head → clears park. That's by design (the machine can still heal a red-head-parked PR by merging main).

For the AC3 fork case: the permission is gone, so refresh can never succeed — every tick burns a full clone+fetch+push against the fork and logs an error, forever, never healing. AC3's intent ("parks guest-style") implies the PR should then wait like a gh-757 park — but gh-757 parks wait for the AUTHOR push because the machine can't push. Here the machine can't push either (permission gone). Yet nothing stops the retry loop. Compare: classic I5 degraded path also retries every tick ("The retry itself stays every-tick (self-healing by design)") — but for the classic path the retry CAN succeed (transient network). For AC3 park, retry can succeed if the author re-enables edits — actually yes! "re-enable 'Allow edits from maintainers'" — the park comment itself tells the author that re-enabling edits + any push clears the park; but actually if the author re-enables edits WITHOUT pushing, the machine's next retry would succeed and move the head, clearing the park automatically. So retry-every-tick is actually the self-healing design and consistent with the classic path philosophy.     "summary": "[GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)",
    "description": "## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

## References

- dmtools-agents#1057 (dead-head park fork-blindness — merged; this card is its update-side sibling)
- Live incident: fa PR #1591, silent-update failures 2026-10-18 19:43–19:47Z, `silent-update-degraded`
- gh-757 (guest park), gh-1000 I5 (silent-update failure bookkeeping)

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e

    "description": "## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e

The lane starts at the top — the gh-994 head-change reset: the parked-head comment records the head sha; head hasn't moved → no reset. Then `forkSilentUpdateGate()`: forkFull non-null, probe → maintainerCanModify true (payload) → `{refresh: true}` → push attempted again → fails → recordForkSilentUpdateFailure: attempt = MAX+1 → no marker; left=0 → label already present → skip park; error log. Indeed the park comment says "ANY push that moves the head (yours, the kicker, a silent main-merge) clears the park" — so the classic lane DOES keep refreshing parked PRs, intentionally: the machine merge moves the head → clears park. AC3's intent ("parks guest-style") implies the PR should then wait like a gh-757 park — but gh-757 parks wait for the AUTHOR push because the machine can't push. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

{
  "key": "gh-1070",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "[GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify; fall back to guest park)",
    "description": "## Goal — fork-aware silent-update: the machine refreshes guest PR heads itself when maintainer-edits allow (v1)

One sentence: **a guest (fork) PR that falls BEHIND main gets its head refreshed by the machine** — base merged into the fork branch via the maintainer-edit push — instead of parking until the guest author happens to push.

Today every lane that touches a PR head is fork-blind in the update direction: silent-update pushes only to the base repo, so for a fork PR it fails 3× (clone/push against a branch that lives in the fork) and flags the PR `silent-update-degraded`; the gh-757 guest park then waits on the human author. Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — branch deleted → dead-head park (fixed in #1057), branch restored but BEHIND → silent-update failed 19:43–19:47Z → `silent-update-degraded` → still parked, human round-trip required.

## Why this framing

- GitHub already grants the capability: on personal-fork PRs "Allow edits from maintainers" is **enabled by default**, and a token with write on the base repo may push to the fork's PR branch (`git push <fork-remote> HEAD:<pr-branch>`). This is a feature gap in the lane, not a platform boundary.
- Retracted framing: "skip fork PRs in silent-update" (from the #1057 discussion) — skipping avoids the failure bookkeeping but keeps the human round-trip; the machine can and should do the update itself when allowed.

## Architecture

- **Probe:** for a cross-repo PR read `maintainerCanModify` (PR payload field) before any silent-update attempt.
- **Allowed path:** clone base, fetch the PR head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` — always fetchable even when the fork branch is deleted), merge `origin/<base>`, push to `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/<fork-owner>/<fork-repo>.git HEAD:<pr-branch>`. Head moves → existing head-change reset clears `validation_failed` / park labels → the standard validate lane resumes. Zero new human protocol.
- **Not-allowed path** (author disabled edits, or org fork — the feature is unavailable there): fall back to the gh-757 guest park exactly as today; NO silent-update attempts and NO failure bookkeeping against such PRs (they can never succeed).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A maintainer-editable fork PR in BEHIND state gets base merged into its fork branch by the machine (head moves, `validation_failed` clears via the existing head-change reset).
- **AC2** — A non-editable fork PR (maintainerCanModify=false) parks without any silent-update attempt, failure marker, or `silent-update-degraded` label.
- **AC3** — Push to the fork fails despite the probe (race: author disabled edits mid-flight) → counted once, next tick re-probes; after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks guest-style (not `silent-update-degraded` — the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **AC4** — Same-repo PRs: zero behavior change (regression guard on the existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — probe routing: editable fork / non-editable fork / same-repo → three distinct paths (pure dispatch function, stubbed scm).
- `UT-2` — editable path builds the fork push URL from `head.repo.full_name` and never targets the base repo for a fork head.
- `UT-3** — non-editable path: no attempt counter increments, park label applied (AC2).
- `IT-1` — simulated BEHIND fork PR: head advances, park label cleared by head-change reset (AC1, end-to-end through the reconcile lane with mocked git).

## Non-goals

- Rework-leg pushes to forks (a leg pushing code changes to a guest's branch is a separate trust/policy decision — this card covers only base-sync merges).
- Requesting broader tokens or the PR author's PAT — maintainer-edits only.

## References

- dmtools-agents#1057 (dead-head park fork-blindness — merged; this card is its update-side sibling)
- Live incident: fa PR #1591, silent-update failures 2026-10-18 19:43–19:47Z, `silent-update-degraded`
- gh-757 (guest park), gh-1000 I5 (silent-update failure bookkeeping)
