**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: case-sensitive same-repo comparison can misroute a base PR into the fork paths**

`forkHeadFull` decides "same repo vs fork" with a case-sensitive string compare:

```javascript
return (full.indexOf('/') !== -1 && full !== baseFull) ? full : null;
```

GitHub repository names are case-insensitive. The base side comes from config (`effectiveRepoInfo.owner/repo`), while `headRepoFull` comes from the API's `head.repo.full_name` — if the two spell the same repository with different casing (e.g. config `istin/dmtools-agents` vs API `IstiN/dmtools-agents`), a **same-repo** PR is classified as a fork:

- AC4 is silently violated (the probe API call is paid, and the refresh goes through the `refs/pull` fetch + merge + `HEAD:<branch>` push instead of the byte-identical base repush).
- Worse: if such a PR carries `maintainer_can_modify=false`, `forkSilentUpdateRoute` sends it to the **park path** — a healthy same-repo PR gets a false guest park and stops receiving validation CI until a human pushes.

This is exactly the class of silent misroute the gh-1059 shared-resolver work was eliminating. Cheap fix — normalize both sides:

```javascript
var full = String(headRepoFull || '').toLowerCase();
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();
```

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: forkSilentUpdateBranch duplicates the classic silent-update command chain**

`forkSilentUpdateBranch` (clone → fetch → ancestor-check → merge → token-URL push) re-implements ~80% of `silentUpdateBranch`'s shell chain a few screens up. The two have already drifted in incidentally (clone shape, comment text) and will keep drifting — e.g. the next silent-update hardening (timeout, depth, `--no-edit` flags, new skip conditions) must be hand-copied to both. Consider extracting one command builder parameterized by (a) how the head is obtained (`--single-branch --branch <b>` vs `refs/pull/<N>/head` fetch) and (b) the push target URL, so the shared ancestor-check/merge/push skeleton exists once.

Same note for `recordForkSilentUpdateFailure`, which mirrors `recordSilentUpdateFailure` — there the divergence is deliberate (guest park vs degraded label), so a shared helper is less pressing, but the marker-trail counting half is identical.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: same-tick double park when the red-head park already fired**

`forkSilentUpdateGate` parks a non-editable fork only when `(ticket.labels || []).indexOf('validation_failed') === -1` — but `ticket.labels` is the **tick-start payload snapshot**. Earlier in this same pass the red-head park (the `headChecksRed` block above) may already have added `validation_failed` and posted its own park comment — the snapshot doesn't reflect that. In that corner (guest fork with red checks AND maintainer edits off) the PR receives **two different park comments in one tick** (label add is idempotent, so no label churn; next tick's fresh payload suppresses further repeats).

Not worth heavy machinery — options: thread the same-pass park state (there is already an `unparkedThisPass` precedent) into the gate, or have `parkForkGuest` skip the comment when the label was added earlier in this pass. Rare corner; comment spam only.

var full = String(headRepoFull || '');
if (full.indexOf('/') === -1) return null;
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();
return full.toLowerCase() !== baseFull ? full : null;

A casing drift between config-derived base (`istin/dmtools-agents`) and the API's `head.repo.full_name` (`IstiN/dmtools-agents`) now resolves to the `base` route for both probe verdicts — no probe API call paid, no `refs/pull` fetch/push, and no false guest park. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: case-sensitive same-repo comparison can misroute a base PR into the fork paths**

`forkHeadFull` decides "same repo vs fork" with a case-sensitive string compare:

```javascript
return (full.indexOf('/') !== -1 && full !== baseFull) ? full : null;
```

GitHub repository names are case-insensitive. The base side comes from config (`effectiveRepoInfo.owner/repo`), while `headRepoFull` comes from the API's `head.repo.full_name` — if the two spell the same repository with different casing (e.g. config `istin/dmtools-agents` vs API `IstiN/dmtools-agents`), a **same-repo** PR is classified as a fork:

- AC4 is silently violated (the probe API call is paid, and the refresh goes through the `refs/pull` fetch + merge + `HEAD:<branch>` push instead of the byte-identical base repush).
- Worse: if such a PR carries `maintainer_can_modify=false`, `forkSilentUpdateRoute` sends it to the **park path** — a healthy same-repo PR gets a false guest park and stops receiving validation CI until a human pushes.

This is exactly the class of silent misroute the gh-1059 shared-resolver work was eliminating. Cheap fix — normalize both sides:

```javascript
var full = String(headRepoFull || '').toLowerCase();
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();
```

## PR Description

Closes #1070
### What changed

`update_branch`'s silent refresh is now fork-aware (gh-1070): a cross-repo PR head is probed for `maintainerCanModify` before any update attempt — an editable fork gets main merged into its fork branch via the maintainer-edit push (`refs/pull/<N>/head` fetch → merge `origin/main` → push `HEAD:<branch>` to the fork's token URL), a non-editable fork parks guest-style with zero attempts and zero bookkeeping, and same-repo PRs ride the untouched base repush.

### Key decisions

- **Pure dispatch** in `validationLiveness` (`forkSilentUpdateRoute` → `base` / `fork` / `park`, `forkPushTokenUrl`) — the three-path routing is unit-testable without scm stubs (UT-1/UT-2); `smAgent` only probes and executes.
- **One shared resolver** `smProvider.ghPrMaintainerCanModify` (REST `maintainer_can_modify` + GraphQL `maintainerCanModify` dialects, `null` when absent) consumed by `githubSource` on the PR item — the gh-1059 no-drift pattern; an unknown probe fails **closed to the park path**, never an unprobed attempt.
- **AC3 race**: a push that fails despite the probe rides the existing silent-update marker trail (counted once per tick, re-probe next tick); after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks **guest-style** (`validation_failed` + `parked-head:` comment) — never `silent-update-degraded` (the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **Park reset parity**: the gh-757 guest park records `parked-head: <sha>`, so the gh-994 head-change reset clears it on any author push; a reset in the same tick yields to the re-query instead of re-parking.
- **AC4**: same-repo heads return `route: 'base'` without even paying the probe API call; the base repush command is byte-identical to the pre-gh-1070 form (regression test pins it).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: case-sensitive same-repo comparison can misroute a base PR into the fork paths**

`forkHeadFull` decides "same repo vs fork" with a case-sensitive string compare:

```javascript
return (full.indexOf('/') !== -1 && full !== baseFull) ? full : null;
```

GitHub repository names are case-insensitive. The base side comes from config (`effectiveRepoInfo.owner/repo`), while `headRepoFull` comes from the API's `head.repo.full_name` — if the two spell the same repository with different casing (e.g. config `istin/dmtools-agents` vs API `IstiN/dmtools-agents`), a **same-repo** PR is classified as a fork:

- AC4 is silently violated (the probe API call is paid, and the refresh goes through the `refs/pull` fetch + merge + `HEAD:<branch>` push instead of the byte-identical base repush).
- Worse: if such a PR carries `maintainer_can_modify=false`, `forkSilentUpdateRoute` sends it to the **park path** — a healthy same-repo PR gets a false guest park and stops receiving validation CI until a human pushes.

This is exactly the class of silent misroute the gh-1059 shared-resolver work was eliminating. Cheap fix — normalize both sides:

```javascript
var full = String(headRepoFull || '').toLowerCase();
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();
```

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1072
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1072
- **Title**: gh-1070 [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify fall back to guest park)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1070` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +842
- **Deletions**: -74
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:56:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T23:24:30Z

## PR Description

Closes #1070
### What changed

`update_branch`'s silent refresh is now fork-aware (gh-1070): a cross-repo PR head is probed for `maintainerCanModify` before any update attempt — an editable fork gets main merged into its fork branch via the maintainer-edit push (`refs/pull/<N>/head` fetch → merge `origin/main` → push `HEAD:<branch>` to the fork's token URL), a non-editable fork parks guest-style with zero attempts and zero bookkeeping, and same-repo PRs ride the untouched base repush.

### Key decisions

- **Pure dispatch** in `validationLiveness` (`forkSilentUpdateRoute` → `base` / `fork` / `park`, `forkPushTokenUrl`) — the three-path routing is unit-testable without scm stubs (UT-1/UT-2); `smAgent` only probes and executes.
- **One shared resolver** `smProvider.ghPrMaintainerCanModify` (REST `maintainer_can_modify` + GraphQL `maintainerCanModify` dialects, `null` when absent) consumed by `githubSource` on the PR item — the gh-1059 no-drift pattern; an unknown probe fails **closed to the park path**, never an unprobed attempt.
- **AC3 race**: a push that fails despite the probe rides the existing silent-update marker trail (counted once per tick, re-probe next tick); after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks **guest-style** (`validation_failed` + `parked-head:` comment) — never `silent-update-degraded` (the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **Park reset parity**: the gh-757 guest park records `parked-head: <sha>`, so the gh-994 head-change reset clears it on any author push; a reset in the same tick yields to the re-query instead of re-parking.
- **AC4**: same-repo heads return `route: 'base'` without even paying the probe API call; the base repush command is byte-identical to the pre-gh-1070 form (regression test pins it).

### How to verify

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js
# full suite (run_all.json manifest): 4531 passed, 0 failed
```

`forkHeadFull` decides "same repo vs fork" with a case-sensitive string compare:

return (full.indexOf('/') !== -1 && full !== baseFull) ? full : null;

GitHub repository names are case-insensitive. - AC4 is silently violated (the probe API call is paid, and the refresh goes through the `refs/pull` fetch + merge + `HEAD:<branch>` push instead of the byte-identical base repush).
- Worse: if such a PR carries `maintainer_can_modify=false`, `forkSilentUpdateRoute` sends it to the **park path** — a healthy same-repo PR gets a false guest park and stops receiving validation CI until a human pushes.

This is exactly the class of silent misroute the gh-1059 shared-resolver work was eliminating. Cheap fix — normalize both sides:

```javascript
var full = String(headRepoFull || '').toLowerCase();
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();

`forkSilentUpdateGate` parks a non-editable fork only when `(ticket.labels || []).indexOf('validation_failed') === -1` — but `ticket.labels` is the **tick-start payload snapshot**. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: case-sensitive same-repo comparison can misroute a base PR into the fork paths**

`forkHeadFull` decides "same repo vs fork" with a case-sensitive string compare:

```javascript
return (full.indexOf('/') !== -1 && full !== baseFull) ? full : null;
```

GitHub repository names are case-insensitive. The base side comes from config (`effectiveRepoInfo.owner/repo`), while `headRepoFull` comes from the API's `head.repo.full_name` — if the two spell the same repository with different casing (e.g. config `istin/dmtools-agents` vs API `IstiN/dmtools-agents`), a **same-repo** PR is classified as a fork:

- AC4 is silently violated (the probe API call is paid, and the refresh goes through the `refs/pull` fetch + merge + `HEAD:<branch>` push instead of the byte-identical base repush).
- Worse: if such a PR carries `maintainer_can_modify=false`, `forkSilentUpdateRoute` sends it to the **park path** — a healthy same-repo PR gets a false guest park and stops receiving validation CI until a human pushes.

This is exactly the class of silent misroute the gh-1059 shared-resolver work was eliminating. Cheap fix — normalize both sides:

```javascript
var full = String(headRepoFull || '').toLowerCase();
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();
```

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1072
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1072
- **Title**: gh-1070 [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify fall back to guest park)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1070` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +842
- **Deletions**: -74
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:56:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T23:24:30Z

## PR Description

Closes #1070
### What changed

`update_branch`'s silent refresh is now fork-aware (gh-1070): a cross-repo PR head is probed for `maintainerCanModify` before any update attempt — an editable fork gets main merged into its fork branch via the maintainer-edit push (`refs/pull/<N>/head` fetch → merge `origin/main` → push `HEAD:<branch>` to the fork's token URL), a non-editable fork parks guest-style with zero attempts and zero bookkeeping, and same-repo PRs ride the untouched base repush.

### Key decisions

- **Pure dispatch** in `validationLiveness` (`forkSilentUpdateRoute` → `base` / `fork` / `park`, `forkPushTokenUrl`) — the three-path routing is unit-testable without scm stubs (UT-1/UT-2); `smAgent` only probes and executes.
- **One shared resolver** `smProvider.ghPrMaintainerCanModify` (REST `maintainer_can_modify` + GraphQL `maintainerCanModify` dialects, `null` when absent) consumed by `githubSource` on the PR item — the gh-1059 no-drift pattern; an unknown probe fails **closed to the park path**, never an unprobed attempt.
- **AC3 race**: a push that fails despite the probe rides the existing silent-update marker trail (counted once per tick, re-probe next tick); after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks **guest-style** (`validation_failed` + `parked-head:` comment) — never `silent-update-degraded` (the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **Park reset parity**: the gh-757 guest park records `parked-head: <sha>`, so the gh-994 head-change reset clears it on any author push; a reset in the same tick yields to the re-query instead of re-parking.
- **AC4**: same-repo heads return `route: 'base'` without even paying the probe API call; the base repush command is byte-identical to the pre-gh-1070 form (regression test pins it).

### How to verify

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js
# full suite (run_all.json manifest): 4531 passed, 0 failed
```

New coverage: routing dialects (UT-1), fork push URL never targets the base (UT-2), non-editable park with zero markers (UT-3/AC2), end-to-end BEHIND fork refresh + park clear (IT-1/AC1), AC3 exhaustion loop over 4 simulated ticks, same-repo regression (AC4), two-fork mixed tick.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: case-sensitive same-repo comparison can misroute a base PR into the fork paths**

`forkHeadFull` decides "same repo vs fork" with a case-sensitive string compare:

```javascript
return (full.indexOf('/') !== -1 && full !== baseFull) ? full : null;
```

GitHub repository names are case-insensitive. The base side comes from config (`effectiveRepoInfo.owner/repo`), while `headRepoFull` comes from the API's `head.repo.full_name` — if the two spell the same repository with different casing (e.g. config `istin/dmtools-agents` vs API `IstiN/dmtools-agents`), a **same-repo** PR is classified as a fork:

- AC4 is silently violated (the probe API call is paid, and the refresh goes through the `refs/pull` fetch + merge + `HEAD:<branch>` push instead of the byte-identical base repush).
- Worse: if such a PR carries `maintainer_can_modify=false`, `forkSilentUpdateRoute` sends it to the **park path** — a healthy same-repo PR gets a false guest park and stops receiving validation CI until a human pushes.

This is exactly the class of silent misroute the gh-1059 shared-resolver work was eliminating. Cheap fix — normalize both sides:

```javascript
var full = String(headRepoFull || '').toLowerCase();
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();
```

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: forkSilentUpdateBranch duplicates the classic silent-update command chain**

`forkSilentUpdateBranch` (clone → fetch → ancestor-check → merge → token-URL push) re-implements ~80% of `silentUpdateBranch`'s shell chain a few screens up. The two have already drifted in incidentally (clone shape, comment text) and will keep drifting — e.g. the next silent-update hardening (timeout, depth, `--no-edit` flags, new skip conditions) must be hand-copied to both. Consider extracting one command builder parameterized by (a) how the head is obtained (`--single-branch --branch <b>` vs `refs/pull/<N>/head` fetch) and (b) the push target URL, so the shared ancestor-check/merge/push skeleton exists once.

Same note for `recordForkSilentUpdateFailure`, which mirrors `recordSilentUpdateFailure` — there the divergence is deliberate (guest park vs degraded label), so a shared helper is less pressing, but the marker-trail counting half is identical.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: same-tick double park when the red-head park already fired**

`forkSilentUpdateGate` parks a non-editable fork only when `(ticket.labels || []).indexOf('validation_failed') === -1` — but `ticket.labels` is the **tick-start payload snapshot**. Earlier in this same pass the red-head park (the `headChecksRed` block above) may already have added `validation_failed` and posted its own park comment — the snapshot doesn't reflect that. In that corner (guest fork with red checks AND maintainer edits off) the PR receives **two different park comments in one tick** (label add is idempotent, so no label churn; next tick's fresh payload suppresses further repeats).

Not worth heavy machinery — options: thread the same-pass park state (there is already an `unparkedThisPass` precedent) into the gate, or have `parkForkGuest` skip the comment when the label was added earlier in this pass. Rare corner; comment spam only.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: duplicated stub property**

```javascript
ghPrHeadRepoFull: smProviderReal().ghPrHeadRepoFull,
ghPrMaintainerCanModify: smProviderReal().ghPrMaintainerCanModify,
ghPrMaintainerCanModify: smProviderReal().ghPrMaintainerCanModify
```

`ghPrMaintainerCanModify` appears twice in this stub object — harmless in JS (last write wins) but it reads as a copy-paste slip and will confuse the next editor. Drop the duplicate line.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: typo in helper name**

`labelAdsDegraded` looks like a slip for `labelAddsDegraded` (it tests the label-**adds** list). The function is hoisted so the test works; renaming keeps the AC3 test readable alongside the `labelAdds` variable it consumes.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

Fixed — `forkHeadFull` (js/common/validationLiveness.js) now lowercases **both sides for the comparison only**:

```javascript
var full = String(headRepoFull || '');
if (full.indexOf('/') === -1) return null;
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();
return full.toLowerCase() !== baseFull ? full : null;
```

A casing drift between config-derived base (`istin/dmtools-agents`) and the API's `head.repo.full_name` (`IstiN/dmtools-agents`) now resolves to the `base` route for both probe verdicts — no probe API call paid, no `refs/pull` fetch/push, and no false guest park. The fork's own canonical casing is preserved in the returned `forkFull` (it builds the maintainer-edit push URL).

Regression tests (both failed before the fix):
- `test_validationLiveness.js` — "the same-repo comparison is CASE-INSENSITIVE": mixed/upper-case drift → `forkHeadFull` null, route `base` with `maintainerCanModify` false **and** true; a genuine mixed-case fork still resolves with its casing intact.
- `test_smAgent.js` — new AC4 variant: item with `headRepo: 'EPAM/Dmtools-Dart'` against lowercase config rides the byte-identical base repush, no probe, zero labels/comments.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

Done — the chain now exists once as `silentUpdateCommand(opts)` in js/smAgent.js, parameterized by exactly the two seams you named:

- `headFlags` / `headSetup` — how the head is materialized: `'--single-branch --branch <b>'` rides the base clone itself; a fork head clones branchless then fetches `refs/pull/<N>/head` and checks it out as the branch.
- `pushTarget` — the full push destination: base token URL + `<branch>` vs the maintainer-edit fork URL + `HEAD:<branch>`.

`silentUpdateBranch` and `forkSilentUpdateBranch` are now thin wrappers; the ancestor-check/merge skeleton and the fa 2026-10-01 root-fix comments live in the builder. The AC4 regression test confirms the base repush stays **byte-identical** to the pre-gh-1070 form.

Two incidental drifts the unification also fixes:
- the fork clone had dropped the documented `gh repo clone … -- <gitflags>` separator — the builder emits `--` for both paths (same form the base path has always used);
- `recordForkSilentUpdateFailure` / `recordSilentUpdateFailure`: the identical marker-trail counting half (one marker per failed tick, capped at MAX) moved into a shared `silentUpdateFailureTrail()`; the deliberate divergence you noted (guest park vs `silent-update-degraded`) stays with the callers, as suggested.

One deliberate non-change: single-quoting the branch name would alter the byte-identical base repush that AC4 pins, so it was left out.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

Fixed via the same-pass state threading you suggested. The red-head park SET block now records `parkedRedHeadThisPass` (the `unparkedThisPass` precedent, park direction), and `parkForkGuest` skips its comment when the flag is set:

```javascript
function parkForkGuest(reason) {
    if (parkedRedHeadThisPass) return;   // red-head park already fired this pass

For a guest fork with red checks AND maintainer edits off, the tick now produces exactly one `validation_failed` add and one park comment (from the red-head park, which already records `parked-head: <sha>`) instead of two different park comments. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

## PR Description

Closes #1070
### What changed

`update_branch`'s silent refresh is now fork-aware (gh-1070): a cross-repo PR head is probed for `maintainerCanModify` before any update attempt — an editable fork gets main merged into its fork branch via the maintainer-edit push (`refs/pull/<N>/head` fetch → merge `origin/main` → push `HEAD:<branch>` to the fork's token URL), a non-editable fork parks guest-style with zero attempts and zero bookkeeping, and same-repo PRs ride the untouched base repush.

### Key decisions

- **Pure dispatch** in `validationLiveness` (`forkSilentUpdateRoute` → `base` / `fork` / `park`, `forkPushTokenUrl`) — the three-path routing is unit-testable without scm stubs (UT-1/UT-2); `smAgent` only probes and executes.
- **One shared resolver** `smProvider.ghPrMaintainerCanModify` (REST `maintainer_can_modify` + GraphQL `maintainerCanModify` dialects, `null` when absent) consumed by `githubSource` on the PR item — the gh-1059 no-drift pattern; an unknown probe fails **closed to the park path**, never an unprobed attempt.
- **AC3 race**: a push that fails despite the probe rides the existing silent-update marker trail (counted once per tick, re-probe next tick); after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks **guest-style** (`validation_failed` + `parked-head:` comment) — never `silent-update-degraded` (the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **Park reset parity**: the gh-757 guest park records `parked-head: <sha>`, so the gh-994 head-change reset clears it on any author push; a reset in the same tick yields to the re-query instead of re-parking.
- **AC4**: same-repo heads return `route: 'base'` without even paying the probe API call; the base repush command is byte-identical to the pre-gh-1070 form (regression test pins it).

node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js
# full suite (run_all.json manifest): 4531 passed, 0 failed
```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests

# Single test suite

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: case-sensitive same-repo comparison can misroute a base PR into the fork paths**

`forkHeadFull` decides "same repo vs fork" with a case-sensitive string compare:

```javascript
return (full.indexOf('/') !== -1 && full !== baseFull) ? full : null;
```

GitHub repository names are case-insensitive. The base side comes from config (`effectiveRepoInfo.owner/repo`), while `headRepoFull` comes from the API's `head.repo.full_name` — if the two spell the same repository with different casing (e.g. config `istin/dmtools-agents` vs API `IstiN/dmtools-agents`), a **same-repo** PR is classified as a fork:

- AC4 is silently violated (the probe API call is paid, and the refresh goes through the `refs/pull` fetch + merge + `HEAD:<branch>` push instead of the byte-identical base repush).
- Worse: if such a PR carries `maintainer_can_modify=false`, `forkSilentUpdateRoute` sends it to the **park path** — a healthy same-repo PR gets a false guest park and stops receiving validation CI until a human pushes.

This is exactly the class of silent misroute the gh-1059 shared-resolver work was eliminating. Cheap fix — normalize both sides:

```javascript
var full = String(headRepoFull || '').toLowerCase();
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();
```

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1072
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1072
- **Title**: gh-1070 [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify fall back to guest park)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1070` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +842
- **Deletions**: -74
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:56:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T23:24:30Z

## PR Description

Closes #1070
### What changed

`update_branch`'s silent refresh is now fork-aware (gh-1070): a cross-repo PR head is probed for `maintainerCanModify` before any update attempt — an editable fork gets main merged into its fork branch via the maintainer-edit push (`refs/pull/<N>/head` fetch → merge `origin/main` → push `HEAD:<branch>` to the fork's token URL), a non-editable fork parks guest-style with zero attempts and zero bookkeeping, and same-repo PRs ride the untouched base repush.

### Key decisions

- **Pure dispatch** in `validationLiveness` (`forkSilentUpdateRoute` → `base` / `fork` / `park`, `forkPushTokenUrl`) — the three-path routing is unit-testable without scm stubs (UT-1/UT-2); `smAgent` only probes and executes.
- **One shared resolver** `smProvider.ghPrMaintainerCanModify` (REST `maintainer_can_modify` + GraphQL `maintainerCanModify` dialects, `null` when absent) consumed by `githubSource` on the PR item — the gh-1059 no-drift pattern; an unknown probe fails **closed to the park path**, never an unprobed attempt.
- **AC3 race**: a push that fails despite the probe rides the existing silent-update marker trail (counted once per tick, re-probe next tick); after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks **guest-style** (`validation_failed` + `parked-head:` comment) — never `silent-update-degraded` (the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **Park reset parity**: the gh-757 guest park records `parked-head: <sha>`, so the gh-994 head-change reset clears it on any author push; a reset in the same tick yields to the re-query instead of re-parking.
- **AC4**: same-repo heads return `route: 'base'` without even paying the probe API call; the base repush command is byte-identical to the pre-gh-1070 form (regression test pins it).

### How to verify

node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js

```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: case-sensitive same-repo comparison can misroute a base PR into the fork paths**

`forkHeadFull` decides "same repo vs fork" with a case-sensitive string compare:

```javascript
return (full.indexOf('/') !== -1 && full !== baseFull) ? full : null;
```

GitHub repository names are case-insensitive. The base side comes from config (`effectiveRepoInfo.owner/repo`), while `headRepoFull` comes from the API's `head.repo.full_name` — if the two spell the same repository with different casing (e.g. config `istin/dmtools-agents` vs API `IstiN/dmtools-agents`), a **same-repo** PR is classified as a fork:

- AC4 is silently violated (the probe API call is paid, and the refresh goes through the `refs/pull` fetch + merge + `HEAD:<branch>` push instead of the byte-identical base repush).
- Worse: if such a PR carries `maintainer_can_modify=false`, `forkSilentUpdateRoute` sends it to the **park path** — a healthy same-repo PR gets a false guest park and stops receiving validation CI until a human pushes.

This is exactly the class of silent misroute the gh-1059 shared-resolver work was eliminating. Cheap fix — normalize both sides:

```javascript
var full = String(headRepoFull || '').toLowerCase();
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();
```

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1072
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1072
- **Title**: gh-1070 [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify fall back to guest park)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1070` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +842
- **Deletions**: -74
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:56:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T23:24:30Z

## PR Description

Closes #1070
### What changed

`update_branch`'s silent refresh is now fork-aware (gh-1070): a cross-repo PR head is probed for `maintainerCanModify` before any update attempt — an editable fork gets main merged into its fork branch via the maintainer-edit push (`refs/pull/<N>/head` fetch → merge `origin/main` → push `HEAD:<branch>` to the fork's token URL), a non-editable fork parks guest-style with zero attempts and zero bookkeeping, and same-repo PRs ride the untouched base repush.

### Key decisions

- **Pure dispatch** in `validationLiveness` (`forkSilentUpdateRoute` → `base` / `fork` / `park`, `forkPushTokenUrl`) — the three-path routing is unit-testable without scm stubs (UT-1/UT-2); `smAgent` only probes and executes.
- **One shared resolver** `smProvider.ghPrMaintainerCanModify` (REST `maintainer_can_modify` + GraphQL `maintainerCanModify` dialects, `null` when absent) consumed by `githubSource` on the PR item — the gh-1059 no-drift pattern; an unknown probe fails **closed to the park path**, never an unprobed attempt.
- **AC3 race**: a push that fails despite the probe rides the existing silent-update marker trail (counted once per tick, re-probe next tick); after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks **guest-style** (`validation_failed` + `parked-head:` comment) — never `silent-update-degraded` (the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone).
- **Park reset parity**: the gh-757 guest park records `parked-head: <sha>`, so the gh-994 head-change reset clears it on any author push; a reset in the same tick yields to the re-query instead of re-parking.
- **AC4**: same-repo heads return `route: 'base'` without even paying the probe API call; the base repush command is byte-identical to the pre-gh-1070 form (regression test pins it).

### How to verify

node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js
# full suite (run_all.json manifest): 4531 passed, 0 failed
```

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: case-sensitive same-repo comparison can misroute a base PR into the fork paths**

`forkHeadFull` decides "same repo vs fork" with a case-sensitive string compare:

```javascript
return (full.indexOf('/') !== -1 && full !== baseFull) ? full : null;
```

GitHub repository names are case-insensitive. The base side comes from config (`effectiveRepoInfo.owner/repo`), while `headRepoFull` comes from the API's `head.repo.full_name` — if the two spell the same repository with different casing (e.g. config `istin/dmtools-agents` vs API `IstiN/dmtools-agents`), a **same-repo** PR is classified as a fork:

- AC4 is silently violated (the probe API call is paid, and the refresh goes through the `refs/pull` fetch + merge + `HEAD:<branch>` push instead of the byte-identical base repush).
- Worse: if such a PR carries `maintainer_can_modify=false`, `forkSilentUpdateRoute` sends it to the **park path** — a healthy same-repo PR gets a false guest park and stops receiving validation CI until a human pushes.

This is exactly the class of silent misroute the gh-1059 shared-resolver work was eliminating. Cheap fix — normalize both sides:

```javascript
var full = String(headRepoFull || '').toLowerCase();
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();
```

## PR Description

### What changed
